_note: Curated emotional backstory bank for Story Research. Players (Heartbreak Files) + countries (Underdog Files). Daily research cross-references these against who scored/played/is trending. Respect caution flags; never use the excluded list.

players.name: Aymen Hussein
players.story: Father (Iraqi army officer) killed by al-Qaeda gunmen in Kirkuk in 2008 when Aymen was 12 — he found the body at the hospital. His older brother, also a soldier, was abducted during the ISIS war and is still missing. Mother told him to play in his father's honour. Iraq's all-time top scorer (34); scored the playoff winner (31 Mar 2026) that sent Iraq to its first WC since 1986, then scored Iraq's lone goal vs Norway.
players.hook: A boy who found his father's body now makes a nation rise.
players.caution: He also scored a stoppage-time own goal vs Norway (Iraq lost 4-1). Brother's disappearance date vague.

players.name: Luka Modrić
players.story: His grandfather (also Luka) was executed by Serb rebels in Dec 1991 and the family home was burned. Six-year-old Luka became a refugee, living for years in a war-battered Zadar hotel, training in the car park to the sound of shelling. Rose to a Ballon d'Or; now 40, likely his final World Cup.
players.hook: A boy who learned football amid gunfire, still running a midfield at 40.

players.name: Cristiano Ronaldo
players.story: Grew up poor in a tin-roofed home in Funchal; his father José Dinis, a war-traumatised ex-soldier, died of liver failure at 52 in 2005. In April 2022 one of his newborn twins, son Ángel, died during childbirth; he keeps Ángel's ashes beside his father's in a home chapel. Chasing a 6th and almost certainly final World Cup.
players.hook: A last dance chasing the one prize missing — carrying a lost father and a lost son.
players.caution: SENSITIVE — death of an infant; handle gently.

players.name: Kalidou Koulibaly
players.story: Captained Senegal to the 2025 AFCON title — then eight days later, on 26 Jan 2026, his father Dabele died in France. His father arrived from Senegal undocumented and worked seven days a week in a textile mill, then as a lumberjack. Cruelly, that AFCON title was later revoked over a walk-off.
players.hook: The captain leading Senegal months after burying the father who sacrificed everything.
players.caution: He missed the AFCON final through suspension (lifted trophy on the podium).

players.name: Edin Džeko
players.story: Six when the Siege of Sarajevo began; his home was destroyed, up to 15 relatives in a 35 m² flat on one meal a day under fire for 1,425 days. One day his mother forbade him from going out and a shell struck the exact spot where he usually played, killing other children. Now 40, captaining Bosnia, his last dance.
players.hook: A boy who survived a siege that killed his playmates, captaining his country at a World Cup.

players.name: Alisson Becker
players.story: On 24 Feb 2021 his father José Agostinho, 57, drowned in a lake near the family's holiday home in southern Brazil. Before the 2026 WC his brother Muriel, also a goalkeeper, wrote him an open letter telling him to 'live our dream.'
players.hook: A clean sheet or decisive save becomes 'for the father who never saw this.'
players.caution: FALSE rumour his brother died — it was his father, by drowning; Muriel is alive.

players.name: Awer Mabil
players.story: Born in the Kakuma refugee camp in Kenya to South Sudanese parents who fled civil war; a decade in the camp before resettling in Adelaide in 2006. In Jan 2019, while away at the Asian Cup, his 19-year-old sister Bor was killed in a car crash. Now a leading refugee advocate.
players.hook: A refugee-camp child who lost his sister mid-tournament once before — a goal is for Bor and every kid in Kakuma.

players.name: Sadio Mané
players.story: His father, the village imam, forbade football then died when Sadio was 7, after having to be carried to a neighbouring village because theirs had no hospital. Ran away to Dakar at 15. Built a hospital and school in Bambali. Says this is his final tournament.
players.hook: A boy who lost his father to a missing hospital now builds them.

players.name: Eduardo Camavinga
players.story: Born 2002 in a refugee camp in Miconge, Cabinda (Angola) after his parents fled Congo's civil war. In 2013 the family home in Fougères burned down, destroying almost everything — fuel to make it as a footballer. France's youngest debutant in over a century.
players.hook: A boy born in a refugee camp whose family lost everything in a fire, now a midfield engine for France.
players.caution: Born in the Cabinda exclave of Angola; some posts oversimplify to 'born in Congo.'

players.name: Riyad Mahrez
players.story: His father, a former amateur footballer, died of a heart attack when Riyad was 15. He chose Algeria over France as a tribute; his hometown Sarcelles named a stadium after him with a plaque bearing his father's name. Algeria captain.
players.hook: The captain who plays for Algeria only to honour the father he lost at 15.

players.name: Endrick
players.story: Extreme poverty in a Brasília suburb (Taguatinga); family often without food and electricity. His father worked janitorial jobs at Palmeiras; the family sold food at a metro station. Vowed to turn pro to feed them — and did, at Real Madrid.
players.hook: A boy who promised to feed his starving family, now scoring at a World Cup for Brazil.
players.caution: 'Orphanage' and 'father slept under ticket booths' trace to secondary sources — soften/attribute.

players.name: Igor Thiago
players.story: Born in Gama; lost his father at 13, then supported his street-cleaner mother as a bricklayer's assistant and market hand. Chose construction over crime. Exploded with 22 Premier League goals for Brentford, earning a maiden Brazil call-up.
players.hook: A bricklayer's boy who buried his father at 13, now on the world's biggest stage.

players.name: Idrissa Gana Gueye
players.story: Youngest of four, played barefoot in working-class Camberene, Dakar. His father — who first spotted his talent and 'taught him everything' — died in 2024.
players.hook: A goal for the father who taught him everything.
players.caution: Exact 2024 death date not confirmed.

players.name: Louicius Don Deedson
players.story: Scored one of the goals that clinched Haiti's first World Cup in over 50 years. His childhood home in Port-au-Prince was partly burned in a 2025 gang attack and relatives fled. Haiti could not play a single qualifier at home.
players.hook: A player whose home was burned by gangs, scoring for a nation that can't safely play at home.

players.name: Esmir Bajraktarević
players.story: Born in Wisconsin to refugee parents who survived the 1995 Srebrenica genocide; grew up American but chose Bosnia, then scored the decisive penalty vs Italy that sent Bosnia to the 2026 WC.
players.hook: The grandson of Srebrenica answers history.
players.caution: Confirm precise penalty/match details against a second report.

players.name: Hakim Ziyech
players.story: His father died of multiple sclerosis when Hakim was 10. Raised by his widowed mother; went off the rails as a grieving teen before football pulled him back. At 14 he first visited his father's grave in Morocco.
players.hook: A grieving boy who nearly lost himself, playing for his father's homeland.
players.caution: Squad inclusion NOT confirmed — verify. Ignore unverified 'brother's death' rumour.

players.name: Granit Xhaka
players.story: His father Ragip was a Kosovar-Albanian political prisoner in Yugoslavia — jailed three and a half years and tortured. Released in 1990, the family fled to Basel; Granit was born there. Switzerland captain.
players.hook: The captain whose father was tortured for his beliefs before fleeing.

players.name: Antonio Rüdiger
players.story: His mother fled the Sierra Leone civil war; raised by six in a Berlin high-rise, parents a caretaker and cleaner. Runs a foundation for war-affected youth in Sierra Leone; UNHCR ambassador.
players.hook: A son of a war refugee anchoring Germany's defence.

players.name: Alireza Beiranvand
players.story: Born into a nomadic Lor family that didn't settle until he was ~12; grew up a shepherd. Ran away to chase football and slept rough in Tehran, taking odd jobs, before becoming Iran's No.1.
players.hook: A homeless shepherd boy now guarding Iran's goal at a World Cup.

players.name: Frantzdy Pierrot
players.story: Born in Cap-Haïtien, raised partly in Massachusetts: 'It was only dirt… we made our own balls with socks filled with trash.' Rose through US college to Europe; the WC is a homecoming for him and a broken country.
players.hook: A boy who played with sock-and-trash balls, leading Haiti's line at a World Cup.

players.name: Édouard Mendy
players.story: Seven years before a World Cup he was unemployed on benefits at 22, partner pregnant, clubless for a year. At the job centre, told to 'think of something else,' he nearly quit — then rebuilt to win the Champions League.
players.hook: A man told by a job centre to give up football, now Senegal's World Cup keeper.

players.name: Nico Williams
players.story: His Ghanaian parents crossed the Sahara on foot to reach Melilla — his mother seven months pregnant with brother Iñaki — robbed of their savings, won asylum via a Caritas priest. Iñaki plays for Ghana; Nico for Spain.
players.hook: A son of parents who crossed a desert on foot, now a Spain star.
players.caution: The 'tore up documents/claimed Liberian' detail is sensitive — verify.

players.name: Mohamed Touré
players.story: Born in a refugee camp in Conakry, Guinea, to Liberian parents displaced by civil war; years in the camp before resettling in Adelaide. Brother Al Hassan is also a Socceroo.
players.hook: A refugee-camp child at a World Cup — camp-to-the-world.

players.name: Romelu Lukaku
players.story: As a boy he came home to find his mother mixing water into milk to stretch it; the family went without electricity and borrowed bread. He vowed to escape poverty through football.
players.hook: 'I remember the days we had no money for milk' — a goal repays that promise to his mother.
players.caution: Confirm he made the final Belgium 26 (injury history).

players.name: Antony
players.story: Grew up in the Osasco favela 'Inferninho' (Little Hell); the home flooded so badly they bailed water at night; drug dealers metres from the door. Scouted at eight doing tricks against grown men.
players.hook: A 'Little Hell' boy at a World Cup — a goal is escape made real.
players.caution: Verify he's in Brazil's 2026 squad and current club.

players.name: Memphis Depay
players.story: His Ghanaian father walked out when Memphis was four; raised by his single mother in struggle. He dropped his father's surname publicly — 'Do not call me Depay, call me Memphis.'
players.hook: A boy abandoned by his father, who erased that name and built his own.
players.caution: Confirm final Netherlands 26 (injury spells).

players.name: Nestory Irankunda
players.story: Born in a refugee camp in Kigoma, Tanzania, to parents who fled Burundi's civil war; moved to Australia as an infant, one of eight in Adelaide, father a rideshare driver. Australia's record A-League export.
players.hook: Refugee-camp-to-World-Cup.
players.caution: Born in TANZANIA, not Burundi (common error).

players.name: Darwin Núñez
players.story: Builder father, milk-hawker mother; moved alone to Montevideo at 14, then a cruciate injury at 17 (two operations). His older brother Junior quit football to provide for the family: 'You're better suited than me.'
players.hook: A goal repays the brother who sacrificed his own dream so Darwin could chase his.

players.name: Moisés Caicedo
players.story: Youngest of 10 in an impoverished Santo Domingo neighbourhood; sold flowers in a cemetery as a child, played barefoot with stones for goalposts. Became a £100m-plus player.
players.hook: A boy who sold cemetery flowers, now anchoring Ecuador's midfield.
players.caution: 'Brothers went without food' is family-anecdote level — soften.

players.name: Enner Valencia
players.story: Deep poverty in San Lorenzo; helped his father sell cow's milk. Too poor for a real ball, his father stitched a rag ball from scavenged cloth. Slept in a room inside a stadium. Ecuador's all-time top scorer and captain.
players.hook: A boy who played with a stitched rag ball, captaining Ecuador.
players.caution: Confirm 2026 squad (age).

players.name: Willian Pacho
players.story: Extreme poverty in Quinindé, one of Ecuador's most violent regions, learning football on dirt. Crossed to Belgium at 20, then Frankfurt, then PSG — first Ecuadorian to win the Champions League (2025).
players.hook: A dirt-pitch boy from a violent region, now a Champions League winner anchoring Ecuador.

players.name: Richarlison
players.story: Eldest of five from a Nova Venécia slum; sold ice cream, washed cars. Walking home from a match he unknowingly crossed a dealer's turf and had a gun pressed to his head — mugged but unhurt.
players.hook: A boy who once had a gun to his head, scoring for Brazil.
players.caution: Gun incident is his own telling. Verify 2026 squad and club.

players.name: James Rodríguez
players.story: When James was three, his father abandoned the family. Raised by his mother and stepfather, moved through three cities, grew up with a stutter. His stepfather bought his first boots. Colombia captain who led 2026 qualification.
players.hook: An abandoned boy with a stutter, now his nation's captain and talisman.
players.caution: Verify father's 'alcoholism' against a primary source; confirm current club.

players.name: Mohamed Salah
players.story: From the poor village of Nagrig, the teenage Salah took up to five buses each way — ~4–5 hours daily — to train in Cairo, leaving school early, getting home at 10pm, for years. Now Egypt's captain and talisman.
players.hook: A boy who rode five buses a day to chase a dream, now the face of Egypt at a World Cup.

players.name: Achraf Hakimi
players.story: Son of Moroccan immigrants in Madrid — a street-vendor father and house-cleaner mother who scraped for his boots. 'They gave up their lives for me.' Morocco captain.
players.hook: A goal 'for the parents who gave up their lives.'
players.caution: Do NOT claim his mother had cancer. He faces a rape charge he denies — keep entirely separate, do not blend.

players.name: Mohammed Kudus
players.story: Raised in Nima, an impoverished Accra slum, by his mother (who ran a roofless open-air food stall) and grandmother; played barefoot on dusty pitches.
players.hook: A Nima slum boy at a World Cup for Ghana.

players.name: Vinícius Júnior
players.story: Grew up on a dead-end street in crime-ridden São Gonçalo, where locals used an app ('Where There's Gunfire') to warn of shootouts. 'I was a kid who only played football barefoot, close to poverty and crime.'
players.hook: A barefoot favela kid who dodged gunfire warnings, now a Real Madrid superstar.
players.caution: Stable family — poverty/violence is context, not personal tragedy.

players.name: Lamine Yamal
players.story: Grew up in Rocafonda, Mataró, where about half the residents are at risk of poverty; named after two men who helped his parents pay rent. His grandmother worked three shifts to bring the family from Morocco. 'A friend would lend us a room.'
players.hook: The teenage prodigy carrying a poor neighbourhood on his back — the '304' Rocafonda gesture.
players.caution: Adversity-overcome, not tragedy — don't overstate.

players.name: Kevin De Bruyne
players.story: At 14–15 the host family he lived with during his Genk academy days refused to take him back, calling him 'too quiet.' He learned of it from his crying mother: 'You threw me in the garbage; now I'm doing well and you want me back?'
players.hook: A boy once 'thrown in the garbage,' now one of the world's best.
players.caution: It was a HOST family, NOT his biological parents — be precise.

players.name: Marcus Rashford
players.story: Raised by a single mother who worked multiple jobs and skipped meals; the family relied on food banks and free school meals. Later forced a UK government U-turn on free school meals.
players.hook: A boy fed by food banks, now feeding a nation's hopes.
players.caution: Confirm he's in England's final 26 (form/loan).

players.name: Bukayo Saka
players.story: After missing the decisive penalty in the Euro 2020 final, the 19-year-old was flooded with racist abuse. He answered with dignity and rose to become one of England's most important players.
players.hook: The boy abused for one penalty, delivering on the biggest stage.

players.name: Luca Zidane
players.story: Zinedine Zidane's son chose Algeria over France through his grandfather. Made his WC debut wearing a protective mask after an April collision left him with a fractured jaw and severe concussion.
players.hook: The famous son carving his own path for Algeria, masked after a frightening injury.

players.name: Vozinha
players.story: The 40-year-old keeper made seven saves to hold mighty Spain, gaining millions of followers overnight — but his mother couldn't attend because of a ~$15,000 US visa bond. After his tearful interview, fees were waived and she flew to Miami to watch him face Uruguay.
players.hook: A clean sheet or penalty save with his mother finally in the stands — the smallest nation ever at a World Cup.
players.caution: Name spelling/age vary across outlets.

players.name: Miguel Almirón
players.story: Born poor in Asunción's San Pablo, father an 18-hour security guard. Rose to MLS and Newcastle, helped fire Paraguay to their first WC since 2010 — then became the first player ever red-carded under the new 'covering the mouth' law.
players.hook: A poverty-to-Premier-League arc with a fresh heartbreak — redemption if he returns.
players.caution: No family death; the red card is a sporting setback, not tragedy.

players.name: Lionel Messi
players.story: At ~10 he was diagnosed with a growth hormone deficiency; treatment was costly and his father's insurance ran out. Argentine clubs wouldn't fund it, forcing the family to Spain, where Barcelona signed the 13-year-old and paid for treatment. Almost certainly his final WC as defending champion.
players.hook: The boy whose body nearly stopped him, ending on the biggest stage.
players.caution: Adversity-overcome, not tragedy.

players.name: Diogo Jota
players.story: Eleven days after marrying his childhood sweetheart Rute, and weeks after winning the Premier League with Liverpool, Jota and his brother André Silva were killed when a tyre blew out on their car on the A-52 near Cernadilla, Spain, 3 July 2025. He was 28, left three children. Portugal carry him as a symbolic 'plus one' with name-and-Jota wristbands.
players.hook: When any Portugal player scores — a look to the sky, a wristband — 'for the angel above their heads.'
players.caution: Deceased — frame as a squad tribute. His number was NOT formally retired; it's the 'plus one'/wristband concept.

players.name: Yan Diomandé
players.story: Grew up with up to 25 people under one roof in Abidjan, marked a fake 'Ronaldo 7' jersey with a black pen, stole potatoes near the Ghana border. Soon after his debut vs Real Madrid at 18 (swapping shirts with Mbappé), his 15-year-old sister Roxane died after, by his account, her drink was spiked. During the WC he published 'Dear Roxane': 'the whole world will know your name.'
players.hook: He plays 'for the angel who guides them from heaven' — watch him sit alone, looking at the sky.
players.caution: Cause of death is the player's own account, not independently confirmed. Spelling varies (Roxane/Roxanne).

players.name: Luis Díaz
players.story: In Oct 2023, while a Liverpool star, ELN guerrillas kidnapped both his parents at a petrol station in Barrancas. His mother was freed within hours; his father was held in the mountains for 12 days. Days in, Díaz scored and revealed 'Libertad para Papá.' Survived a childhood of indigenous Wayuu poverty (nicknamed 'Fideo' — Noodle).
players.hook: A son who begged the world for his father's freedom now plays without fear — watch him point skyward.

players.name: João Neves
players.story: Lost his mother Sara Gonçalves to cancer in Feb 2024 when he was 19 at Benfica. Widely told he called her after every match and promised to win the Champions League for her; when PSG won it in 2025 he wept and turned his face to the sky. Dedicates his first senior goals to her.
players.hook: If Neves scores, he looks up — to his mother. 'This one he can only tell the sky.'
players.caution: The 'called her after every match' detail traces to fan retellings — not a hard quote.

players.name: Raúl Jiménez
players.story: On 29 Nov 2020 he fractured his skull in a clash with David Luiz, lay motionless, had emergency surgery, and was written off for nearly two years (returned in a protective headguard). His father died in March 2026; he wept after scoring days later. Scored Mexico's second in a 2-0 home WC opener vs South Africa — his first WC goal.
players.hook: The comeback header in the opener, dedicated to his late father.
players.caution: 'Back in training within two weeks' is FALSE — recovery took months.

players.name: Alphonso Davies
players.story: Born in the Buduburam refugee camp in Ghana after his parents fled the Second Liberian Civil War; resettled in Canada at ~five. Canada's greatest-ever player and captain — then tore his ACL vs the USA in March 2025, a 221-day recovery and muscle injuries leaving his home-WC place hanging by a thread.
players.hook: A refugee-camp baby captaining the host nation — if he steps on after that injury hell, it's a triumph.
players.caution: Born in GHANA, not Liberia. Don't claim he 'starred in the opener.'

players.name: Giovanni Reyna
players.story: Son of USMNT legend Claudio Reyna; lost his older brother Jack to a brain tumour in 2012 — Jack was 13. Channelled the grief into football despite injuries and a 2022 WC fallout; fought back into the 2026 squad.
players.hook: If Reyna scores for the hosts, it's for the big brother he lost at 13.
players.caution: No verified depression diagnosis for Gio himself — don't claim that.

players.name: Álvaro Morata
players.story: Spain's captain revealed he battled severe depression, panic attacks and suicidal ideation before Euro 2024 — and considered faking an injury to skip it. Helped by the team doctor and Iniesta, he then lifted the trophy as captain.
players.hook: A captain who nearly walked away from the game lifting his country — mental-health survival made visible.
players.caution: Verify current club and 2026 squad inclusion.

players.name: Jonathan David
players.story: Born in Brooklyn to Haitian parents, raised in Ottawa; his mother died of cancer in Dec 2019 when he was 19 and starting out in Belgium. Dedicates goals and squad numbers to her.
players.hook: A goal for the mother who died just as his career began — points to the sky.

players.name: Davinson Sánchez
players.story: Born in Caloto, Cauca — scarred by 50+ years of FARC conflict. From age 10 he travelled two hours each way alone to train because the family couldn't afford two fares. Many childhood friends died or were jailed in drug crime. 'The Rock of Caloto.'
players.hook: A boy from a war-torn town whose friends didn't make it out — escape rewarded.

players.name: Franck Kessié
players.story: His father — an ex-pro turned soldier — died of illness when Franck was 11, deepening hardship and a move to rough Yopougon, Abidjan. Grew up during civil war, rode buses up to three hours to training.
players.hook: A goal for the soldier-father he lost at 11.
players.caution: Father-death-at-11 lightly sourced — corroborate. The 'siblings died in a fire' claim is FALSE.

players.name: Gabriel Jesus
players.story: Lost his father young; his mother Vera Lúcia raised four children alone as a cleaner in the São Paulo favela Jardim Peri. As a teen he painted the favela's streets for the 2014 WC. His phone-celebration mimics calling his mother.
players.hook: The phone celebration — a goal is a call to the mother who cleaned houses to raise him.
players.caution: 'Lost father shortly after birth' timing varies. Confirm final 26.

players.name: Ronwen Williams
players.story: When he was 18, his older brother Marvin was killed in a head-on car crash in April 2010. He nearly quit. He now looks to the sky and 'talks to' Marvin, his guardian angel, and captained South Africa back to the WC.
players.hook: A penalty save or clean sheet from the captain — a glance skyward to his brother.
players.caution: Correct version: brother Marvin, car crash, when Ronwen was 18 (NOT 'shot at age 10').

players.name: Emiliano Martínez
players.story: Deep poverty in Mar del Plata; his mother told the boys 'your dad and I aren't hungry — you eat' when rice ran short; his truck-driver father wept over unpaid bills. Left home at 17. Became a World Cup-winning keeper.
players.hook: A penalty save carries the kid who left home hungry at 17.

players.name: Raphinha
players.story: Raised in the violent Restinga favela amid daily gunfire, sharing one bedroom, sometimes going hungry. Rejected by Grêmio at nine for being underdeveloped. Clawed his way to Barcelona.
players.hook: A goal is the favela kid once turned away for being 'too small.'
players.caution: Gunfire/begging details are his own accounts — present as 'he has said.'

players.name: Sofiane Boufal
players.story: Born in Paris to Moroccan parents, raised mainly in Angers by a single mother who cleaned. His father died in Aug 2019 after a long illness.
players.hook: A goal for the father he lost in 2019.
players.caution: Confirm current club and 2026 squad — status uncertain.

players.name: Lyle Foster
players.story: From working-class Noordgesig near Soweto, where his father quit his job to back him. After moving to Europe he battled severe depression (disclosed 2023) and took an indefinite leave for treatment, then recovered to lead South Africa's attack.
players.hook: A goal from a man who stepped away from football to save himself, and came back.
players.caution: Confirm final-squad inclusion.

players.name: Mike Maignan
players.story: Born in French Guiana, raised in the Paris suburbs. As AC Milan's keeper he was racially abused at Udinese in Jan 2024 and led his team off the pitch, becoming a leading anti-racism voice.
players.hook: A clean sheet from a keeper who refused to play through racist abuse — dignity rewarded.
players.caution: Verify 2026 France squad (GK competition).

players.name: Alexander Isak
players.story: Born in Solna to Eritrean refugees who fled the Eritrean–Ethiopian war; runs youth football projects in Eritrea.
players.hook: A goal honours the parents who fled a war so he could be born free.
players.caution: Confirm Sweden's 2026 qualification/squad.

players.name: Xherdan Shaqiri
players.story: Born in Gjilan, Kosovo; family fled to Switzerland when he was ~four, settling near Basel in an unheated farmhouse. Father washed dishes then did road construction; mother cleaned offices.
players.hook: A goal from the refugee boy raised in an unheated farmhouse.
players.caution: Confirm 2026 Switzerland squad (veteran).

players.name: Breel Embolo
players.story: Born in Cameroon, family migrated via France to Basel. Suffered multiple severe injuries (incl. ACL). At 18 founded a foundation for refugee children and disadvantaged youth.
players.hook: A goal from a migrant kid who kept rebuilding his body and his story.
players.caution: 'Refugee' is loose (economic migration). Verify squad.

players.name: Tajon Buchanan
players.story: Broke his tibia in a Canada session at Copa América (July 2024) — 'I truly felt like my career was finished.' Returned in ~4 months, moved to Villarreal and scored a La Liga hat-trick.
players.hook: A goal from a man who thought a broken leg had ended him.
players.caution: Verify final 26.

players.name: Ousmane Dembélé
players.story: Raised by a single immigrant mother, Fatimata, after his father left; she took odd jobs. He dedicated his 2025 Ballon d'Or to her: 'This is for you, Mama.'
players.hook: A goal for the mother who raised him alone — now a Ballon d'Or winner.

players.name: Tim Weah
players.story: Son of George Weah, whose prime was wrecked by Liberia's civil war, denying him a World Cup. Tim fulfilled that dream, scoring for the USA at the 2022 WC.
players.hook: A goal completes the World Cup story his legendary father never got to write.

players.name: Casemiro
players.story: His father left when he was five; his mother Magda raised three children alone in poverty in São José dos Campos. He once wept recalling he couldn't afford a yoghurt drink. Bought his mother a house with his first earnings.
players.hook: A goal for the mother who raised three kids alone.

players.name: Ismaël Bennacer
players.story: Born in Arles, raised in rough Trinquetaille 'where lots of young people end up selling drugs.' His father immigrated from Morocco at 20, was illiterate, did back-breaking construction, and pushed education as the way out.
players.hook: A goal for the illiterate labourer father who demanded his son escape.
players.caution: Confirm current club and Algeria squad.

players.name: Chancel Mbemba
players.story: One of nine children raised amid the poverty and wars of 1990s–2000s Kinshasa, learning football barefoot. Now captain leading DR Congo's historic World Cup return.
players.hook: The captain of a war-shadowed nation's historic return — a goal is collective catharsis.
players.caution: Confirm Mbemba's club/squad.

players.name: Federico Valverde
players.story: From working-class Unión, Montevideo — casino-guard father, flea-market-vendor mother. Two years before joining Real Madrid at 17 he slept on a 'sandwich bed' on the floor. 'In Uruguay, hardship is in our blood.'
players.hook: A goal from the boy who slept on a floor mattress before Madrid.

players.name: Edson Álvarez
players.story: From Tlalnepantla; family made football kits. Released by Pachuca at 10 for being too short; made Club América after a three-month tryout, with a daily 3–4 hour round trip eating most of his wage.
players.hook: A goal from the kid told he was too small, who spent his wages just getting to training.
players.caution: Host nation — verify 26.

players.name: Hirving Lozano
players.story: Born in Mexico City with scarce resources; father worked odd jobs; grew up on cracked concrete. Football lifted the family out of poverty.
players.hook: A goal from the boy off the cracked concrete pitch, now a host-nation star.
players.caution: Poverty detail mostly from aggregators; verify host-Mexico squad.

players.name: Jérémy Doku
players.story: Antwerp-born to Ghanaian parents who emigrated in 1993; father did construction; family struggled to pay fees and buy boots. Took a Ghanaian passport in 2025.
players.hook: A goal for the construction-worker father who scraped to pay the fees.

players.name: Denzel Dumfries
players.story: Rotterdam-born to an Aruban father and Surinamese mother; family briefly emigrated to Aruba but returned over money. Mocked as a youth for poor technique; willed himself into a top pro.
players.hook: A goal from the kid everyone said wasn't technical enough.

players.name: Takefusa Kubo
players.story: First Japanese boy to pass Barcelona's La Masia test — then, when FIFA sanctioned Barça, 13-year-old Kubo was barred and forced out of Spain. 'You don't know why they've kicked you out… I still don't know why.' Rebuilt and returned.
players.hook: A goal from the boy exiled from his dream club at 13, through no fault of his own.

players.name: Julio Enciso
players.story: From rural Caaguazú, raised in his grandfather's house; street-vendor father, cleaner mother. Bought his parents a house at 17. Stretchered off in tears with a double leg injury a week before Paraguay's opener.
players.hook: The homeless kid who bought his family a house, refusing to miss his World Cup.
players.caution: FITNESS DOUBT — injured close to the opener; verify he plays.

players.name: Bruno Guimarães
players.story: Son of a Rio taxi driver (dispatch No. 39, which he wears as tribute). 'My father drove a yellow taxi day and night so I could have a ham-and-cheese sandwich.' Rejected by Botafogo and Fluminense.
players.hook: A goal honours the taxi-driver father — the No. 39 is the tell.

players.name: Ronald Araújo
players.story: Raised in humble Mandubí, Rivera, with food scarcity; father worked away in forestry, Brazilian mother cleaned and sold fried pastries at his first club.
players.hook: A clean sheet for the mother who sold pastries to keep him in football.

players.name: Pervis Estupiñán
players.story: Afro-Ecuadorian from Esmeraldas, one of the poorest regions; sold meat pies as a boy to fight poverty.
players.hook: A goal/assist from the boy who sold pies on the street.

players.name: Youssef En-Nesyri
players.story: From a football-loving family in Fez; started as a barefoot street footballer before King Mohammed VI's academy for street-connected children took him in.
players.hook: A goal from the barefoot alley kid of Fez.
players.caution: 'Poor neighbourhood' vs 'middle-class Fez family' appears inconsistently.

players.name: Amine Harit
players.story: Grew up in Pontoise — 'toward the end of some months there wouldn't be enough to go around' — in an unsafe neighbourhood. Chose Morocco out of debt to family in Casablanca.
players.hook: A goal for the family who went without at month's end.
players.caution: Verify 2026 squad (injury history).

players.name: Nicolas Jackson
players.story: Gambian-born, grew up in Banjul amid the 2016 Gambian political crisis; family relocated to Ziguinchor, Senegal in 2017. Learned the game informally without academies.
players.hook: A goal from the self-taught kid who left Gambia amid political chaos.
players.caution: No verified father-death. Birthplace disputed. Confirm club/loan.

players.name: Antoine Semenyo
players.story: Rejected by Arsenal, Spurs, Fulham, Millwall and Crystal Palace; at 15 he cried in his dad's car ('why does this keep happening?') and quit for a year, before rebuilding via college and the lower leagues. Father drove a taxi in South London.
players.hook: A goal from the boy who quit at 15 after everyone rejected him.
players.caution: 'Homeless/trampoline job' claims are unfounded. Confirm club and Ghana squad.

players.name: Mohammed Salisu
players.story: As a teen reportedly denied a Ghana U-17 call-up because his family couldn't pay the fee, then over a year clubless before a trial revived his career.
players.hook: A clean sheet from the boy frozen out because his family couldn't pay.
players.caution: Pay-to-play claim is single-source (family interview).

players.name: Patrik Schick
players.story: A €30m Juventus move (2017) collapsed after he failed the medical over a reported heart issue at 21 — a career-jeopardising scare. Rebuilt at Roma and Leverkusen.
players.hook: A goal from a man once failed on a heart scan at 21.
players.caution: Heart issue reported, never fully detailed — don't overstate. Verify Czechia squad.

players.name: Lucas Paquetá
players.story: Grew up on tiny Paquetá Island in Rio (~3,000 residents), taking daily ferries plus four buses to training with his grandfather until the family left when he was 11.
players.hook: A goal from the island boy who ferried hours to chase the game.
players.caution: Modest, not poverty. Faces an FA betting probe — not an emotional hook.

players.name: Cédric Bakambu
players.story: Born in the Paris banlieue to DRC immigrants; grew up speaking Lingala but had never set foot in Congo — his arc is reconnecting with an ancestral homeland.
players.hook: A goal for the homeland he only discovered as an adult.
players.caution: Identity/roots arc, not hardship.

players.name: Iliman Ndiaye
players.story: Only boy among seven sisters; left the Marseille academy when the family moved to Senegal, training three years on Dakar's beaches before clawing up through English non-league to the PL.
players.hook: A goal from the boy who trained on Dakar's beaches and rose through non-league.

players.name: Folarin Balogun
players.story: Born in Brooklyn by chance (his Nigerian mother was barred from flying home to London while pregnant), raised in London; chose the USA over England and Nigeria.
players.hook: An identity-and-belonging arc — a goal for the country he chose.

players.name: Weston McKennie
players.story: An 'army brat' who discovered football aged five near Ramstein Air Base, Germany, during his father's USAF service.
players.hook: A goal from the military kid who found football on a German base.

players.name: Kylian Mbappé
players.story: Raised in working-class, immigrant-heavy Bondy by a Cameroonian coach father and Algerian-Kabyle ex-handball-pro mother — a banlieue-to-superstar arc on family discipline. France captain.
players.hook: A goal is Bondy-to-the-world for the captain.
players.caution: Don't overstate Bondy as extreme poverty — stable family.

players.name: Randal Kolo Muani
players.story: Born in Bondy to parents from Kinshasa, DR Congo; raised with strict discipline (his father pulled him back from Italy to finish school).
players.hook: A goal for the immigrant family that prized his schooling first.
players.caution: Thin emotional hook. Verify France squad.

players.name: Kaoru Mitoma
players.story: Turned down a pro contract at 18, went to university and wrote a famous thesis on dribbling (wearing a GoPro), before exploding into the PL.
players.hook: A dazzling dribble-and-goal pays off the boy who studied the art of beating defenders.

players.name: Lee Kang-in
players.story: After a clash with captain Son Heung-min at the 2023 Asian Cup he was vilified, then flew to London to apologise in person and made a televised apology; Son praised his courage; he reintegrated.
players.hook: A goal is the redemption of a player who owned a very public mistake.
players.caution: Self-inflicted controversy + redemption. The Valencia 'bullying' rumours are disputed — do NOT use.

players.name: Christian Pulisic
players.story: USA captain from Hershey, PA; a Croatian grandfather's passport let him move to Dortmund at 16. Has spoken about the loneliness and mental toll of early fame.
players.hook: As captain and talisman, any decisive goal is the story — the emotional hook is thinner.
players.caution: No real adversity. A 2026 injury doubt was reported — verify fitness.

players.name: Aurélien Tchouaméni
players.story: Of Cameroonian descent; his father, a pharmacist, failed to make it as a pro and poured that dream into his son. Stable, educated family.
players.hook: A goal carries a father's lost footballing dream — but the hook is soft.

players.name: Marcel Sabitzer
players.story: Son of ex-Austria international Herfried Sabitzer: 'I got 50 percent of his mentality and 50 percent of his talent — I've had to work for the rest.' Part of Austria's first WC squad since 1998.
players.hook: A goal completes the family arc — and Austria's long-awaited return.

countries.name: Haiti
countries.story: Reached its first World Cup in over 50 years while the nation collapsed — armed gangs control much of Port-au-Prince, so the team could not play a single home qualifier, staging them in Curaçao. Clinched with a 2-0 win over Nicaragua in Nov 2025; the poorest country in the Americas erupted in rare collective joy.
countries.hook: A team with no home just gave a nation in chaos something to believe in.
countries.caution: Say 'much of the capital,' not exact gang-control percentages. Lost opener 0-1 to Scotland (12 June 2026).

countries.name: Uzbekistan
countries.status: Debutant — first ever (first Central Asian nation)
countries.story: First Central Asian nation to qualify, ~47 years after the 1979 Pakhtakor Tashkent air disaster that killed 17 players/staff and shadowed Uzbek football for decades. The 'White Wolves,' coached by Fabio Cannavaro, completed the journey their predecessors never could.
countries.hook: 47 years after a disaster took their best team, the White Wolves finally arrived.
countries.caution: Pakhtakor died as a Soviet CLUB, not the national team — frame as 'football culture's defining tragedy.'

countries.name: Curaçao
countries.status: Debutant — smallest nation EVER to qualify
countries.story: An island of ~156,000 became the smallest nation ever at a World Cup, beating Iceland's record, unbeaten across qualifying, largely built from the Dutch diaspora. Legendary coach Dick Advocaat stepped away in Feb 2026 to care for his ailing daughter (returned in May).
countries.hook: 156,000 people. One island. The smallest nation ever to reach a World Cup.
countries.caution: Population figures vary 152–160k.

countries.name: Cape Verde
countries.story: An archipelago of ~525,000 shaped by drought, famine and emigration (more Cape Verdeans abroad than home) reached its first World Cup at the seventh attempt. The 'Blue Sharks' are a diaspora team; first WC goal by Kevin Pina (21 June 2026); drew Spain 0-0 and Uruguay 2-2.
countries.hook: A scattered people, a tiny island chain — and finally, a place at the world's table.
countries.caution: 'Smallest' now belongs to Curaçao — Cape Verde is among the smallest, not THE smallest.

countries.name: DR Congo
countries.story: The Leopards returned after 52 years, exorcising the ghosts of 1974. They got there through a brutal playoff gauntlet — beating Cameroon, edging Nigeria on penalties, then Jamaica in extra time — against the backdrop of one of the world's deadliest ongoing conflicts in the country's east.
countries.hook: 52 years and a brutal playoff road later, the Leopards are back.
countries.caution: Keep the conflict reference general and respectful.

countries.name: Jordan
countries.story: Jordan reached its first-ever World Cup after a stunning run to the 2023 Asian Cup final. A kingdom of ~11 million hosting huge refugee populations. Clinched on an Ali Olwan hat-trick; Olwan scored Jordan's first WC goal vs Austria.
countries.hook: From Asian Cup finalists to World Cup debutants — a small kingdom's giant leap.
countries.caution: Refugee-host angle is backdrop only.

countries.name: Iraq
countries.story: Iraq returned after 40 years — only its second appearance — for a nation whose football has been repeatedly disrupted by war and sanctions, and which won the 2007 Asian Cup amid violence as an act of unity. Survived a stoppage-time penalty and a 2-1 win over Bolivia.
countries.hook: Forty years and countless dark days later, the Lions of Mesopotamia are back.
countries.caution: Don't conflate with the 2007 Asian Cup era. Lost 1-4 to Norway.

countries.name: South Africa
countries.story: Bafana Bafana returned for the first time since hosting in 2010 — a 16-year wait — overcoming a three-point deduction for an ineligible player, sealing it with a 3-0 win over Rwanda ahead of Nigeria. Coach Hugo Broos.
countries.hook: Sixteen years after they hosted the world, South Africa is back at the party.
countries.caution: They qualified DESPITE the deduction, not because of a reversal.

countries.name: Scotland
countries.story: Scotland ended a 28-year exile. Seemingly dead and buried, they were rescued by results elsewhere, then beat Denmark 4-2 with a McTominay overhead kick and two stoppage-time stunners. Opened 2026 beating Haiti 1-0 — first WC finals win since 1990.
countries.hook: Twenty-eight years of hurt, undone in one impossible night.
countries.caution: A famous footballing nation — 'underdog' is about the drought, not minnow status.

countries.name: Bosnia & Herzegovina
countries.story: Bosnia returned for the first time since their 2014 debut — a country forged from the 1990s Balkan war and the siege of Sarajevo. Captain Edin Džeko, a child of that war, now 40, leads them in his last dance. Qualified via playoffs over Wales (pens) and Italy.
countries.hook: A nation born from war, led one last time by its favourite son.
countries.caution: Keep Džeko's wartime childhood accurate; avoid embellishment.

countries.name: New Zealand
countries.story: The All Whites reached their third World Cup and first since 2010 (when they went home unbeaten with three draws). In a rugby-mad country they rode Oceania's first guaranteed direct slot, going a perfect 5-0 with 29 goals.
countries.hook: From rugby's shadow, the All Whites claim Oceania's first guaranteed seat at the table.
countries.caution: 2010 'unbeaten' is true but they didn't advance — phrase precisely.

countries.name: Norway
countries.story: Norway returned after 28 years — their generational talent Erling Haaland wasn't born when they last appeared. Perfect qualifying (8 wins), beating Italy, Haaland 16 goals. Also the 'sons of 1994' — Haaland, Sørloth and Thorstvedt are sons of the 1994 squad.
countries.hook: Norway hadn't been to a World Cup since before Haaland was born. Now he's leading them there.
countries.caution: Player-led, less 'tragic' — the nation angle is the 28-year absence.

countries.name: Côte d'Ivoire
countries.status: Dark horse — reigning African champions, first since 2014
countries.story: The Elephants returned after 12 years as reigning African champions, having won the 2023 AFCON on home soil in a fairy-tale comeback. Hungry to finally translate continental dominance onto the world stage.
countries.hook: African champions, back on the world stage to break a 12-year curse.
countries.caution: Reigning African champions — a dark horse, not a true minnow. Lost 1-2 to Germany.

countries.name: Panama
countries.story: Panama qualified for only their second-ever World Cup, finishing top of their final group unbeaten. Their 2018 debut was so emotional the president declared a national holiday.
countries.hook: Once a national holiday, now a habit — Panama proves it belongs.

countries.name: Algeria
countries.story: The Desert Foxes returned after missing 2018 and 2022 — a proud nation that reached the round of 16 in 2014 and whose 1982 win over West Germany is etched in lore. Sealed with a 3-0 win in Somalia.
countries.hook: The Desert Foxes are back to recapture the magic of '82 and '14.
countries.caution: A traditional African power — underdog by recent absence, not a minnow.

countries.name: Tunisia
countries.status: Perennial — 7th WC, never past the group
countries.story: Tunisia reached a 7th World Cup (3rd straight) after a dominant campaign — nine wins, one draw, no goals conceded in 10 matches. In 1978 they were the first African side to win a WC match, yet have never escaped the group across six appearances.
countries.hook: Six World Cups, never past the group — can the Carthage Eagles finally break through?

countries.name: Iran
countries.status: Perennial — 4th straight, never past the group
countries.story: Iran qualified for a fourth straight World Cup amid acute US–Iran tensions; the team was based in Tijuana and faced severe US travel restrictions, reportedly allowed in only around match days. Never advanced past the group.
countries.hook: Playing under restrictions and the world's glare, Team Melli chase a first-ever knockout berth.
countries.caution: Sensitive — report travel restrictions factually, avoid editorialising on the conflict.

countries.name: Ghana
countries.story: The Black Stars qualified again after missing 2018 and exiting early in 2022. Ghana carries the pain of Asamoah Gyan's missed penalty vs Uruguay in 2010, when they came within a kick of becoming the first African semifinalists.
countries.hook: Still chasing the African dream that slipped away in 2010.
countries.caution: The 2010 Gyan story is a past memory — frame as motivation.

countries.name: Paraguay
countries.story: Paraguay returned for the first time since 2010, ending a 16-year exile for a fiercely passionate nation that reached the quarterfinals on its last appearance. Ground back through the brutal South American qualifiers.
countries.hook: Sixteen years in the wilderness — Paraguay's grit drags them back to the big stage.
countries.caution: Talisman Miguel Almirón red-carded early in the tournament.

countries.name: Egypt
countries.story: Egypt — the most successful nation in African football history (record AFCON titles) — returned after missing 2022, qualifying with a game to spare via a 3-0 win over Djibouti, often with Mohamed Salah leading the line.
countries.hook: Africa's record champions return to chase an overdue World Cup moment.
countries.caution: Continental royalty — underdog only at World Cup level.

countries.name: Austria
countries.story: Austria qualified directly by winning their group, ending a long World Cup absence (last 1998). A proud old footballing nation of the 1930s 'Wunderteam' era finally returns.
countries.hook: Austria ends a generation in the World Cup wilderness.
countries.caution: The absence is World-Cup-specific — they've reached Euros in between.

countries.name: Czechia
countries.story: Czechia returned for the first time since 2006, surviving playoffs — penalties past Ireland, then a shootout over Denmark. A nation with a glorious past (Euro 1996 finalists) ending a two-decade exile.
countries.hook: Twenty years on, Czechia returns from the cold.
countries.caution: Distinguish Czech Republic from Czechoslovakia history.

countries.name: Qatar
countries.story: Qatar qualified on merit for the first time, having previously appeared only as 2022 hosts (lost all three — worst host record ever). Topped their fourth-round Asian group.
countries.hook: No longer the host with the worst record — Qatar earns its way in.
countries.caution: Wealthy and well-resourced — an underdog only in football terms.

countries.name: Saudi Arabia
countries.story: Saudi Arabia qualified for a 7th World Cup — the nation that beat Argentina 2-0 in 2022. Future hosts of 2034. Clinched via a 0-0 draw with Iraq.
countries.hook: The team that toppled Argentina is back — and hosting is next.
countries.caution: Well-resourced future hosts — only a sporting underdog.

countries.name: Australia
countries.story: The Socceroos reached a 6th consecutive World Cup (7th overall), their first automatic qualification since 2014, in a country where football fights for oxygen against rugby, cricket and AFL. Sealed with a come-from-behind 2-1 over Saudi Arabia.
countries.hook: Against the odds and the other codes, the Socceroos keep showing up.
countries.caution: Reliable qualifier — frame around the 'other codes' angle, not minnow status.

excluded: Sébastien Haller (left out of the final 26)
Ismaël Koné (a sporting injury, not a personal-tragedy backstory)
Thomas Partey (active criminal allegations — controversy, not a backstory)
Son Heung-min (father's child-abuse conviction — uncomfortable, not a clean tragedy arc)
Mehdi Taremi (middle-class upbringing; not a poverty arc)
